recall.minute: Traditional software encodes rules written by developers, with logic in code and bugs fixed by editing it; ML learns rules from data, so logic lives in parameters, the goal is generalisation and fixes often involve data, features or training. Good code has five features: simplicity (DRY, no needless complexity), modularity (logical functions with clear inputs and outputs), readability (PEP 8 or the Google style guide, good names, docstrings, enforced by pylint), performance and robustness (reproducible, runs end to end, handles errors, logs, is tested). Python gets faster through better algorithms and data structures, vectorised built-ins, asynchronous I/O and parallelism. Measure with timeit, which repeats runs and reports mean ± standard deviation, rather than a single time.time() reading. Profile with cProfile (ncalls, tottime, cumtime) to find slow functions and line_profiler to find slow lines, such as fit at 62.7% of runtime, and use memray or memory_profiler for memory.
